topic: 3-1 The Overall Structure of Web Applications

questions.question: A web application is composed of three tiers. The screen component that users see directly is the (a). Server-side processing that users do not see is the (b). A system that stores, organizes, and manages data is the (c). Fill in the blanks (a)–(c).
The frontend is the screen component that users see and interact with directly.
The backend is responsible for server-side processing that users do not see.
The database is the part of a web application that users directly see and interact with.
For each item, indicate which tier it belongs to: A Frontend, B Backend, C Database.
From the following options, choose the one that most appropriately describes the frontend.
options: A system that stores and manages data
The screen component users see and interact with directly
Server-side processing that users do not see
A system that makes decisions about stored data
questions.answer: The screen component users see and interact with directly

questions.question: A user searches for a product. Complete the flow: The frontend receives the search keywords and sends them to the (a). The backend searches the (b). The database returns matching data. The backend organizes the result and the frontend (c) the result.
Explain how the frontend, backend, and database cooperate when a user searches for a product.
questions.answer: The frontend receives the search keywords and sends them to the backend. The backend searches the database. The database returns matching data to the backend. The backend organizes the result and sends it to the frontend, which displays the result.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate role of the database?
options: Accepting user input and displaying results
Displaying the web page in the browser

questions.question: Think as an Engineer — A clinic wants a web application where patients can book appointments, check available time slots, and view their past visits. Which tier should handle each task, and why?
questions.answer: The frontend handles the booking screen and user input. The backend processes the booking request and checks available slots. The database stores and retrieves appointment and visit information.

questions.question: New Context — A weather application allows users to enter a city and view weather information. Using the three-tier architecture, describe what the frontend, backend, and database could do.
questions.answer: The frontend collects the city name and displays the weather. The backend processes the request and obtains the required weather data. The database can store and retrieve relevant information such as user or historical weather data.

questions.question: Reflect & Challenge — Why must the frontend, backend, and database cooperate instead of performing all tasks in one part of the application?
questions.answer: Each tier has a different responsibility. Separating them makes the application easier to understand, develop, maintain, and troubleshoot.
